requirements.quote:
The packet number is an integer in the range 0 to 2^62-1.  This
   number is used in determining the cryptographic nonce for packet
   protection.  Each endpoint maintains a separate packet number for
   sending and receiving.
requirements.condition: For every packet number.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the packet number as an integer from 0 through 2^62-1 inclusive.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a packet number outside the inclusive range 0 to 2^62-1.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation test can inspect generated or accepted packet-number values and verify the inclusive numeric bounds.

requirements.quote:
The packet number is an integer in the range 0 to 2^62-1.  This
   number is used in determining the cryptographic nonce for packet
   protection.  Each endpoint maintains a separate packet number for
   sending and receiving.
requirements.condition: At each endpoint.
requirements.required_behavior: Maintain separate packet-number state for sending and receiving.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a single shared packet-number state for both sending and receiving.
requirements.why_checkable: State inspection or bidirectional traffic tests can verify that send-side and receive-side packet-number state are independent.

requirements.quote:
Packet numbers are limited to this range because they need to be
   representable in whole in the Largest Acknowledged field of an ACK
   frame (Section 19.3).  When present in a long or short header,
   however, packet numbers are reduced and encoded in 1 to 4 bytes; see
   Section 17.1.
requirements.condition: When a packet number is present in a long or short header.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the reduced packet number in 1 to 4 bytes inclusive.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode the header packet-number field using zero bytes or more than four bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: Serialized long and short headers can be parsed to measure the packet-number field length.

requirements.quote:
Version Negotiation (Section 17.2.1) and Retry (Section 17.2.5)
   packets do not include a packet number.
requirements.condition: For a Version Negotiation or Retry packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not include a packet number.
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized forms of Version Negotiation and Retry packets can be inspected for absence of a packet-number field.

requirements.quote: Packet numbers are divided into three spaces in QUIC:
requirements.condition: For QUIC packet-number state.
requirements.required_behavior: Divide packet numbers into exactly three packet number spaces.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation's packet-number state and packet-type mappings can be inspected to verify that three spaces are defined.

requirements.quote:
Initial space:  All Initial packets (Section 17.2.2) are in this
      space.
requirements.condition: For every Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Place the packet in the Initial packet number space.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place an Initial packet in another packet number space.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet classification can be tested by observing which packet-number state is used for Initial packets.

requirements.quote:
Handshake space:  All Handshake packets (Section 17.2.4) are in this
      space.
requirements.condition: For every Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Place the packet in the Handshake packet number space.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place a Handshake packet in another packet number space.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet classification can be tested by observing which packet-number state is used for Handshake packets.

requirements.quote:
Application data space:  All 0-RTT (Section 17.2.3) and 1-RTT
      (Section 17.3.1) packets are in this space.
requirements.condition: For every 0-RTT or 1-RTT packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Place the packet in the application data packet number space.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place a 0-RTT or 1-RTT packet in the Initial or Handshake packet number space.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet classification and packet-number state can be inspected for both 0-RTT and 1-RTT packets.

requirements.quote:
Conceptually, a packet number space is the context in which a packet
   can be processed and acknowledged.  Initial packets can only be sent
   with Initial packet protection keys and acknowledged in packets that
   are also Initial packets.  Similarly, Handshake packets are sent at
   the Handshake encryption level and can only be acknowledged in
   Handshake packets.
requirements.condition: When sending an Initial packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send an Initial packet using protection keys from another encryption level.
requirements.why_checkable: Cryptographic instrumentation or test keys can verify which protection keys are used to protect an Initial packet.

requirements.quote:
Conceptually, a packet number space is the context in which a packet
   can be processed and acknowledged.  Initial packets can only be sent
   with Initial packet protection keys and acknowledged in packets that
   are also Initial packets.  Similarly, Handshake packets are sent at
   the Handshake encryption level and can only be acknowledged in
   Handshake packets.
requirements.condition: When acknowledging an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Carry the acknowledgment in an Initial packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not acknowledge an Initial packet in a non-Initial packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Generated acknowledgments can be correlated with received Initial packets and checked for their enclosing packet type.

requirements.quote:
Conceptually, a packet number space is the context in which a packet
   can be processed and acknowledged.  Initial packets can only be sent
   with Initial packet protection keys and acknowledged in packets that
   are also Initial packets.  Similarly, Handshake packets are sent at
   the Handshake encryption level and can only be acknowledged in
   Handshake packets.
requirements.condition: When sending a Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Send it at the Handshake encryption level.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send a Handshake packet at another encryption level.
requirements.why_checkable: Cryptographic instrumentation or packet traces can verify the encryption level used for Handshake packets.

requirements.quote:
Conceptually, a packet number space is the context in which a packet
   can be processed and acknowledged.  Initial packets can only be sent
   with Initial packet protection keys and acknowledged in packets that
   are also Initial packets.  Similarly, Handshake packets are sent at
   the Handshake encryption level and can only be acknowledged in
   Handshake packets.
requirements.condition: When acknowledging a Handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Carry the acknowledgment in a Handshake packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not acknowledge a Handshake packet in a non-Handshake packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Generated acknowledgments can be correlated with received Handshake packets and checked for their enclosing packet type.

requirements.quote:
This enforces cryptographic separation between the data sent in the
   different packet number spaces.  Packet numbers in each space start
   at packet number 0.  Subsequent packets sent in the same packet
   number space MUST increase the packet number by at least one.
requirements.condition: When initializing any packet number space.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not initialize the space's packet-number sequence to a value other than 0.
requirements.why_checkable: The first packet emitted in each packet number space can be decoded and checked for packet number 0.

requirements.quote:
This enforces cryptographic separation between the data sent in the
   different packet number spaces.  Packet numbers in each space start
   at packet number 0.  Subsequent packets sent in the same packet
   number space MUST increase the packet number by at least one.
requirements.condition: For each subsequent packet sent in the same packet number space.
requirements.required_behavior: Increase its packet number by at least one relative to the preceding packet sent in that space.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not keep the packet number unchanged or decrease it within that packet number space.
requirements.why_checkable: A sequence of sent packets can be grouped by packet number space and checked for a strictly increasing packet number.

requirements.quote:
0-RTT and 1-RTT data exist in the same packet number space to make
   loss recovery algorithms easier to implement between the two packet
   types.
requirements.condition: For 0-RTT and 1-RTT data in a connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the same packet number space for both packet types.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not maintain separate packet number spaces for 0-RTT and 1-RTT data.
requirements.why_checkable: Traffic containing both packet types can be inspected to verify that they share one packet-number sequence and acknowledgment context.

requirements.quote:
A QUIC endpoint MUST NOT reuse a packet number within the same packet
   number space in one connection.  If the packet number for sending
   reaches 2^62-1, the sender MUST close the connection without sending
   a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame or any further packets; an endpoint MAY send
   a Stateless Reset (Section 10.3) in response to further packets that
   it receives.
requirements.condition: Within one packet number space in one connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reuse a packet number.
requirements.why_checkable: All sent packet numbers can be grouped by connection and packet number space and checked for uniqueness.

requirements.quote:
A QUIC endpoint MUST NOT reuse a packet number within the same packet
   number space in one connection.  If the packet number for sending
   reaches 2^62-1, the sender MUST close the connection without sending
   a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame or any further packets; an endpoint MAY send
   a Stateless Reset (Section 10.3) in response to further packets that
   it receives.
requirements.condition: If the sending packet number reaches 2^62-1.
requirements.error_behavior: Terminate the connection when the sending packet-number limit is reached.
requirements.why_checkable: A boundary test can drive sending state to 2^62-1 and observe whether the connection closes.

requirements.quote:
A QUIC endpoint MUST NOT reuse a packet number within the same packet
   number space in one connection.  If the packet number for sending
   reaches 2^62-1, the sender MUST close the connection without sending
   a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame or any further packets; an endpoint MAY send
   a Stateless Reset (Section 10.3) in response to further packets that
   it receives.
requirements.condition: When closing because the sending packet number reached 2^62-1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame.
requirements.error_behavior: Close silently without a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A boundary test can capture outbound traffic during closure and verify absence of a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame.

requirements.quote:
A QUIC endpoint MUST NOT reuse a packet number within the same packet
   number space in one connection.  If the packet number for sending
   reaches 2^62-1, the sender MUST close the connection without sending
   a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame or any further packets; an endpoint MAY send
   a Stateless Reset (Section 10.3) in response to further packets that
   it receives.
requirements.condition: After the sending packet number reaches 2^62-1 and the sender closes the connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send any further packets, except that a Stateless Reset may be sent in response to a further received packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Post-limit traffic can be captured to verify that no further ordinary packets are emitted and that any emission is only an allowed response.

requirements.quote:
A QUIC endpoint MUST NOT reuse a packet number within the same packet
   number space in one connection.  If the packet number for sending
   reaches 2^62-1, the sender MUST close the connection without sending
   a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame or any further packets; an endpoint MAY send
   a Stateless Reset (Section 10.3) in response to further packets that
   it receives.
requirements.condition: If an endpoint receives further packets after closing because its sending packet number reached 2^62-1.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint may respond with a Stateless Reset.
requirements.why_checkable: A post-closure input test can determine whether any optional response that is produced is a Stateless Reset.

requirements.quote:
A receiver MUST discard a newly unprotected packet unless it is
   certain that it has not processed another packet with the same packet
   number from the same packet number space.  Duplicate suppression MUST
   happen after removing packet protection for the reasons described in
   Section 9.5 of [QUIC-TLS].
requirements.condition: When a receiver has newly removed packet protection but is not certain that it has not already processed a packet with the same packet number from the same packet number space.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not process the packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Duplicate and ambiguous-duplicate inputs can be injected and receiver processing can be observed to verify discard behavior.

requirements.quote:
A receiver MUST discard a newly unprotected packet unless it is
   certain that it has not processed another packet with the same packet
   number from the same packet number space.  Duplicate suppression MUST
   happen after removing packet protection for the reasons described in
   Section 9.5 of [QUIC-TLS].
requirements.condition: When performing duplicate suppression.
requirements.required_behavior: Remove packet protection before checking for and suppressing duplicates.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not perform duplicate suppression before removing packet protection.
requirements.why_checkable: Instrumented packet processing or focused duplicate tests can verify the ordering of unprotection and duplicate detection.

requirements.quote:
The data required for detecting duplicates can be limited by
   maintaining a minimum packet number below which all packets are
   immediately dropped.  Any minimum needs to account for large
   variations in round-trip time, which includes the possibility that a
   peer might probe network paths with much larger round-trip times; see
   Section 9.
requirements.condition: If an endpoint maintains a minimum packet number to limit duplicate-detection state.
requirements.required_behavior: Immediately drop every packet whose packet number is below that minimum.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not process a packet whose packet number is below the maintained minimum.
requirements.why_checkable: A configured or observed minimum can be paired with below-threshold packet inputs to verify immediate dropping.

requirements.quote:
The data required for detecting duplicates can be limited by
   maintaining a minimum packet number below which all packets are
   immediately dropped.  Any minimum needs to account for large
   variations in round-trip time, which includes the possibility that a
   peer might probe network paths with much larger round-trip times; see
   Section 9.
requirements.condition: If an endpoint chooses a minimum packet number for duplicate detection.
requirements.required_behavior: Account for large round-trip-time variations, including probes on paths with much larger round-trip times.
requirements.why_checkable: The passage does not define a numeric bound or algorithm for determining whether the minimum adequately accounts for round-trip-time variation.
